A.
History and Development of the Company
GDEV Inc. (formerly, Nexters Inc.), “GDEV” or the “Issuer”, is a business company incorporated under the laws of the British Virgin Islands on January 27, 2021. GDEV was formed for the sole purpose of effectuating the Transactions contemplated by the Business Combination Agreement, including the merger of Kismet Acquisition One Corp. (“Kismet”) into the Issuer and the acquisition by the Issuer of all of the issued and outstanding share capital of Nexters Global Ltd. (“Nexters Global”). The Transactions were consummated on August 26, 2021.
Upon the closing of the Transactions, the Issuer became the direct parent of Nexters Global, a developer of mobile, web, and social games. For an overview of the history of Nexters Global, see “ —B. Business Overview—Our History .”
On June 21, 2023, GDEV filed a Certificate of Name Change with the Registrar of Corporate Affairs of the British Virgin Islands to change its name from “Nexters Inc.” to “GDEV Inc.” The name change was effective as of the date of filing of the

Certificate of Name Change. The name change reflects the evolution of the Company as a holding company focused on the growth of its diversified portfolio of studios and franchises.
On December 19, 2023, the Company launched a tender offer to purchase for cash (as adjusted for the Reverse Share Split) a minimum of 1,500,000 of its ordinary shares, up to a maximum of 2,000,000 ordinary shares, at a purchase price of $20.00 per share (the “Tender Offer”). The Tender Offer expired on January 18, 2024, resulting in the Company’s accepting for purchase 1,655,425 shares. The shares acquired pursuant to the Tender Offer are held by the Company as treasury shares.
On August 8, 2024, the board of directors of the Company approved by written resolution a one-for-ten (1:10) reverse share split of the Company’s ordinary shares (the “Reverse Share Split”). The Reverse Share Split became effective at 4:01 p.m. Eastern Time on August 28, 2024. Upon effectiveness of the Reverse Share Split, the Company’s ordinary shares trade under a new CUSIP number, G6529J209.
On September 12, 2024, the Company entered into a Sales Agreement (the “Sales Agreement”) with Cantor Fitzgerald & Co. and Oppenheimer & Co. Inc. (together, the “Agents”), under which it may offer and sell, from time to time, 1,757,026 ordinary shares of the Company, held in treasury (including all shares acquired pursuant to the Tender Offer), through a designated Agent in an “at the market offering” (the “ATM Offering”), as defined in Rule 415(a)(4) promulgated under the Securities Act. Sales under the ATM Offering may be made directly on or through Nasdaq, in negotiated transactions at market prices prevailing at the time of sale or at prices related to such prevailing market prices and/or any other method permitted by law. During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company sold a total of 214 ordinary shares for an aggregate amount of $ 5,384.70 under the ATM Offering. The Company did not sell any ordinary shares under the ATM Offering in the year ended December 31, 2025.

B.
Business Overview
Overview
We build mobile, web and social games for millions of players to enjoy globally. Our games are free to play, and we continuously innovate our games to provide novel, curated in-game content to our users at optimal points in their game journeys.
Our core product offering, Hero Wars, offers a suite of games across mobile, social and web-based platforms and has, since its launch in 2016, evolved into a well-recognized global gaming franchise in the RPG genre, with 5.4 million MAUs across more than 70 countries in 2025. In 2025, Hero Wars was ranked the 2 nd most downloaded game in the RPG genre on Android and iOS, combined, according to data provided by AppMagic.
Continuous improvements in game content and focus on customer engagement has allowed us to monetize on the popularity of our games and achieve attractive key performance metrics. In particular as of December 31, 2025, Hero Wars’ cumulative all time Bookings crossed the $2.5 billion mark. We benefit from predictable cohorts and a loyal base of core players, which supports our ability to sustain our monetization per user. In the year ended December 31, 2025, cohorts from previous periods accounted for 68.9% of our Bookings for our core product, Hero Wars.
Since our formation over a decade ago, we have developed a sizeable built-to-scale platform, enabling us to streamline content development and offering a value-enhancing opportunity for our new and existing games. In 2022, we entered into agreements to acquire four separate gaming studios to expand our portfolio of mid-core games, enlarge our player base and expand into new genres. We plan to further expand gameplays within our current products as well as work towards new game offerings.
Our headquarters are in Cyprus. As of December 31, 2025, we had 488 employees. Our revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 was $404.3 million and $420.9 million, respectively, and our Bookings 2 for the same periods were

Our Industry
We operate in the global digital gaming market, a significant and growing component of the entertainment industry. Mobile gaming represents the largest segment of the global games market, accounting for approximately 55% of total global gaming revenue according to Newzoo. According to Sensor Tower, mobile gaming IAP revenue on iOS and Google Play reached approximately $81.75 billion in 2025, marking the third consecutive year of revenue growth despite a continued decline in downloads, pointing to a market that is increasingly driven by deeper monetization of existing players rather than expansion of the player base.
Total mobile gaming downloads across iOS and Google Play declined to approximately 50.4 billion in 2025 according to Sensor Tower, continuing a multi-year downward trend. Despite this, total hours spent in mobile gaming continued to grow, reflecting sustained player engagement among existing users according to Sensor Tower. According to Sensor Tower, IAP revenue growth was approximately 1% year-over-year in 2025 on a mobile games basis, with growth skewed toward Europe while the United States remained essentially flat.
Genre performance in 2025 was highly uneven. According to Sensor Tower, strategy games drove the largest revenue gains across all major regions, with meaningful IAP revenue growth in Asia, North America and Europe year-over-year, powered largely by titles from publishers headquartered in China and other Asia-Pacific markets. RPG, by contrast, continued to face significant headwinds, with IAP revenue declining across Asia, North America and Europe year-over-year. Downloads fell across casual, mid-core and hybrid-casual product models, while hybrid-casual was the standout monetization gainer, with IAP revenue growing sharply while casual and mid-core remained essentially flat.
The competitive landscape among publishers shifted meaningfully in 2025. According to Sensor Tower, publishers headquartered in Asia-Pacific markets materially increased their share of global mobile IAP revenue year-over-year, while North American publishers experienced a decline. The mobile gaming advertising market also underwent structural change, with video ad formats and rewarded placements growing their share of total impressions, while advertising spend continued to consolidate toward a smaller number of dominant networks.
Looking ahead, Sensor Tower projects continued growth in mobile gaming revenue, driven by improving monetization strategies, a stronger focus on player retention and lifetime value, and ongoing engagement growth in key markets including the United States and Japan, where time spent rebounded in 2025 following declines in 2024.

We rely on third-party distribution platforms, such as the iOS App Store, Facebook, and Google Play Store, to distribute our games and collect revenues generated on such platforms, and rely on third-party payment processors, such as Xsolla, to collect certain web-based revenues, and such platforms and payment processors may adversely change their policies.
●
Our core game offering, Hero Wars, generates a substantial portion of our revenue.
●
A small percentage of total users have generated a majority of our revenues.
●
Our free-to-play business model, and the value of virtual items sold in our games, is highly dependent on how we manage the game revenues and pricing models.

●
We operate in a highly competitive industry with low barriers to entry.
●
Legal or regulatory restrictions or proceedings could adversely impact our business and limit the growth of our operations.

Risks Related to the Company’s Business and Operations
We rely on third-party distribution platforms, such as the iOS App Store, Facebook, Huawei and Google Play Store, to distribute our games and collect revenues generated on such platforms, and rely on third-party payment processors, such as Xsolla, to collect certain web-based revenues, and such platforms and payment processors may adversely change their policies.
Our games are primarily accessed and operated through distribution platforms such as Apple, Facebook, Google, and Huawei AppGallery, which serve as significant online distribution channels for our games. In addition, we rely on third-party payment processing and merchant-of-record solutions, such as Xsolla, for revenues generated through our web browser channel. Substantially all of the virtual items that we or our distributors sell to paying players are purchased using the payment processing systems of these platforms. Consequently, our prospects and expansion depend on our continued relationships with these providers, and any other emerging platform providers that are widely adopted by our target players. We and our distributors are subject to the standard terms and conditions of these platform providers for application developers, which govern the content, promotion, distribution, operation of games and other applications on their platforms, as well as the terms of the payment processing services provided by the platforms, and which the platform providers can change unilaterally with little or no notice. Our business would be harmed if:
●
the platform providers discontinue or limit our or our distributors’ access to their platforms;
●
governments or private parties, such as internet providers, impose bandwidth restrictions or increase charges or restrict or prohibit access to those platforms;
●
governments or private parties impose restrictions, prohibitions or conditions in relation to payments;
●
the platforms increase the fees they charge us or our distributors;
●
the platforms modify their algorithms, communication channels available to developers, respective terms of service or other policies;
●
the platforms decline in popularity;
●
the platforms adopt changes or updates to their technology that impede integration with other software systems or otherwise require us to modify our technology or update our games in order to ensure players can continue to access our games and content with ease;
